senses.gloss: part. Hif. of <cite ref="N01392"><he>נָתַר</he></cite> q. v.
that which makes an object permitted for enjoyment.
units: Zeb. II, 3 המ׳ the blood (the sprinkling of which makes the sacrifice fit for eating or for the altar); a. fr.—Pl. מַתִּירִים, מַתִּירִין.

<cite ref="Mishnah Zevachim 4:3">Ib. IV, 3</cite>; <cite ref="Mishnah Meilah 2:9">Meïl. II, 9</cite> <he>כל שיש לו מ׳</he> whatever may become permitted through a certain act, e. g. the meal-offering by taking a handful for the altar.

<cite ref="Mishnah Meilah 2:9">Ib.</cite> <he>מַתִּירָיו</he> those things which cause it to be available. Ib. 10ᵇ <he>דבר שיש לו מ׳ אינו חייב עד שיקרבו מ׳</he> a thing (sacrificial object) which requires an act to make it permissible, is not subject to <cite ref="M02111"><he>מְעִילָה</he></cite>, until the things by which it is made available have been offered on the altar.—
<cite ref="Beitzah 3b:9">Bets. 3ᵇ</cite> <he>דבר שיש לו מ׳</he> a thing which may become permitted (being prohibited only for the day).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 53a:2">B. Mets. 53ᵃ</cite> <he>הוה ליה דבר שיש לו מ׳</he> it would be considered a thing which can be made fit (by redemption); a. fr.
